name: claude-activity-viewer
description: VS Code extension that surfaces your Claude Code agents live in a sidebar — a read-only activity viewer driven by Claude Code hooks. See running sub-agents, their model and context usage, and recent sessions, without leaving the editor.

commands.title: Claude Activity Viewer: Rescan projects and sessions
Claude Activity Viewer: Install global activity hooks
Claude Activity Viewer: Uninstall global activity hooks

claudeActivityViewer.projectsRoot.description: Absolute paths. Each direct subfolder of a path here is treated as a project. Used to derive project/task labels in the dashboard from the agent cwd. Tildes (~) are expanded to the user home.

claudeActivityViewer.scannerRefreshSec.description: Auto-refresh interval (seconds) for the project + session scanner. 0 disables auto-refresh (default) — use the 'Rescan' button in the dashboard toolbar or the 'Rescan projects and sessions' command. Re-scanning re-parses every .jsonl from disk; with many projects (50+) keep this at 0 to avoid recurring I/O spikes.

claudeActivityViewer.resumeConfirm.description: If true, show a confirmation dialog before resuming a past Claude session.

claudeActivityViewer.notifyOnComplete.description: If true, show a VS Code notification toast when an agent finishes (done / failed / cancelled). Click 'Open detail' on the toast to jump to the detail panel.

claudeActivityViewer.ingesterDebug.description: If true, log every translated agent event from the global hook stream to the output channel. The viewer ingests events regardless of this flag; it only controls verbose diagnostics.

enumDescriptions: Open the resumed session in the Claude Code sidebar chat (requires the 'anthropic.claude-code' extension). Falls back to terminal if the extension is missing.
Open the resumed session in a new VS Code terminal running 'claude --resume <id>'.
claudeActivityViewer.resumeIn.description: Where to open a past session when clicking Resume. 'chat' uses the Claude Code extension's URI handler; 'terminal' spawns a new VS Code terminal.

scripts.compile: npm run compile:extension && npm run compile:webview
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck:extension && npm run typecheck:webview
scripts.package: npm run typecheck && node esbuild.config.mjs --production && vite build
